title: Get started
text: {strainselect} helps choosing bacterial strains sequence collection described metadata (sampling context, matrix, region, sector, year…). offers two complementary methods: clustering method (assess_gower(), cstats_table(), select_silhouette()) suited number strains can sequenced limited. Strains grouped k clusters similar strains best clustered strain cluster selected, selected strains different possible ; profile method (prepare_upset(), define_profiles(), select_profiles()) suited number strains sequence limited. Strains sharing exactly metadata grouped one strain per group selected, every distinct profile — including unique strains — represented. methods start prepare_input(), cleans raw table. examples use salmonella_strains, table 100 Salmonella strains described 22 variables, shipped package. selection based 6 variables: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT year extracted DATE_PRELEVEMENT.

title: Get started
text: using methods, dataset must cleaned contain metadata selection based. prepare_input(): checks strain identifiers unique (stops list duplicated identifiers otherwise); uses identifiers row names; keeps selected metadata columns; optionally extracts year (ANNEE) /month (MOIS) date column; replaces missing values "unknown" converts every column factor. Columns can given names (recommended, easier read depend order columns) positions. Dates read date_format, "%d/%m/%Y" (e.g. 09/01/2020) default; use instance date_format = "%Y-%m-%d" dates 2020-01-09. date column already class Date used .

title: Get started
text: clustering method uses three functions: assess_gower(), cstats_table() select_silhouette(). cstats_table() optional number strains sequence fixed advance.

title: Get started
text: assess_gower() computes dissimilarity matrix strains using Gower distance, suited categorical metadata. Weights can given metadata adjust importance clustering. hierarchical clustering complete linkage performed matrix, dendrogram drawn graph = TRUE.
code: raw_data <- salmonella_strains prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),                                id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT") #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = TRUE)

what: Choosing the number of clusters: cstats_table
title: Get started
text: cstats_table() computes clustering statistics (see fpc::cluster.stats()) increasing number clusters: step, 2 * step, …, k. average silhouette width (avg.silwidth) useful one: plotted number clusters, optimal number clusters marked maximum plateau curve. idea test large number clusters without exceeding number strains can sequenced; larger step reduces computing time.  small step (every 2 clusters), curve shows two plateaus. average silhouette width jumps 0.45 16 clusters stays 0.39 0.43 30 clusters: 15 clusters first level already captures main structure collection. jumps 0.47 34 clusters stays 0.47 0.51 52 clusters: 33 clusters second, finer level. Beyond, curve increases number distinct profiles (61), every profile isolated: categorical metadata, maximum natural level grouping. number strains sequence can chosen one two plateaus, depending resources available.
code: raw_data <- salmonella_strains prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),                                id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT") #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE) stats <- cstats_table(dist = gower$gower_dist, tree = gower$aggl.clust.c,                       k = 60, step = 2) #> testing 2 clusters #> testing 4 clusters #> testing 6 clusters #> testing 8 clusters #> testing 10 clusters #> testing 12 clusters #> testing 14 clusters #> testing 16 clusters #> testing 18 clusters #> testing 20 clusters #> testing 22 clusters #> testing 24 clusters #> testing 26 clusters #> testing 28 clusters #> testing 30 clusters #> testing 32 clusters #> testing 34 clusters #> testing 36 clusters #> testing 38 clusters #> testing 40 clusters #> testing 42 clusters #> testing 44 clusters #> testing 46 clusters #> testing 48 clusters #> testing 50 clusters #> testing 52 clusters #> testing 54 clusters #> testing 56 clusters #> testing 58 clusters #> testing 60 clusters

title: Get started
text: last step selects one strain sequence cluster. number clusters k either chosen silhouette plot set number strains can sequenced. cluster, strain largest silhouette width — .e. best clustered strain — selected. several strains share largest silhouette width cluster, one chosen random; use seed make choice reproducible.

what: Selecting strains for a sequencing budget: select_strains
title: Get started
text: select_strains() runs whole clustering method one step answers practical question “can sequence n_max strains: ones?”. computes Gower distances clustering tree (assess_gower()), average silhouette width every number clusters 2 number distinct profiles. number clusters largest average silhouette width optimal number clusters k_opt. budget (n_max = NULL): one strain per optimal cluster, .e. k_opt strains, status "optimal"; budget larger optimum (n_max >= k_opt): k_opt optimal strains, completed n_max strains (status "supplementary") cutting tree n_max clusters. Use fill = FALSE stop optimum. clusters nested, supplementary strain comes cluster contain optimal strain yet; budget smaller optimum (n_max < k_opt): tree cut n_max clusters one strain selected (status "selected"). optimal groups represented selected strain listed, user knows missed. cluster, selected strain one largest silhouette width, .e. best clustered one (ties broken random, use seed reproducibility). categorical metadata equal weights, identical strains distance 0 optimum often close number distinct profiles: supplementary strains mostly metadata already selected strains, add replicates rather diversity. general rule. weights change Gower distances different strains, hence tree, silhouette curve optimum (example vignette, weight 3 REGION lowers optimum 61 22 clusters), supplementary strains can add new profiles. Conversely, optimum, strains cluster similar identical. report written report_selection() gives, actual data, number supplementary strains metadata already selected strain, much strains differ selected strain cluster. select_strains(method = "profile") applies logic profile method. strains identical metadata form groups, sorted decreasing size (groups size random order); one strain per group optimal selection: budget smaller number groups: one strain n_max largest groups — frequent profiles favoured, smallest groups (often strains unique profile) listed represented; budget larger number groups: one strain per group, supplementary strains added turn turn — second strain group one, largest group smallest, third strain, . Within group, strains metadata chosen random (use seed reproducibility).
code: prepared_data <- prepare_input(   salmonella_strains,   col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),   id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT" ) #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE # clustering method, no budget: optimal number of strains res <- select_strains(prepared_data, seed = 1) res #> Strain selection (clustering method) #>   strains: 100 - distinct profiles: 61  #>   optimal number of clusters (k_opt): 61  #>   maximum number of strains (n_max): not given #>   selected strains: 61 (optimal: 61) plot(res) # budget smaller than the optimum res_20 <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 20, seed = 1) res_20 #> Strain selection (clustering method) #>   strains: 100 - distinct profiles: 61  #>   optimal number of clusters (k_opt): 61  #>   maximum number of strains (n_max): 20  #>   selected strains: 20 (selected: 20)  #>   optimal groups not represented: 41 out of 61 head(res_20$table[, c("cluster", "optimal_group", "selected", "status")]) #>               cluster optimal_group selected       status #> 2020LSAL00151       1             1    FALSE not selected #> 2020LSAL00152       1             1    FALSE not selected #> 2020LSAL00163       2             2    FALSE not selected #> 2020LSAL00167       2             3    FALSE not selected #> 2020LSAL00176       3             4    FALSE not selected #> 2020LSAL00177       3             5     TRUE     selected # profile method, budget larger than the number of distinct profiles res_profile <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 75, method = "profile", seed = 1) res_profile #> Strain selection (profile method) #>   strains: 100 - distinct profiles: 61  #>   groups of identical strains: 61  #>   maximum number of strains (n_max): 75  #>   selected strains: 75 (optimal: 61, supplementary: 14) plot(res_profile) head(res_profile$groups) #>   group size n_selected #> 1     1   10          2 #> 2     2    7          2 #> 3     3    5          2 #> 4     4    4          2 #> 5     5    3          2 #> 6     6    3          2 #>                                                                                                                                                    profile #> 1                                                             Alerte Produit | Viande de dinde | Pays de la Loire | Alimentation humaine | Abattage | 2020 #> 2                     Alerte Produit | Bovins | Auvergne Rhone Alpes | Santé et production animales | Lieu d'exploitation, d'élevage, ou de culture | 2020 #> 3                                          Surveillance | Viande de dinde | Nouvelle Aquitaine | Alimentation humaine | Transformation industrielle | 2020 #> 4                                   Surveillance | Viande porcine | Provence Alpes Cote d Azur | Alimentation humaine | Transformation industrielle | 2020 #> 5 Programmes de contrôle et d'éradication | Gallus gallus | Bretagne | Santé et production animales | Lieu d'exploitation, d'élevage, ou de culture | 2020 #> 6                                                            Surveillance | Viande de canard | Nouvelle Aquitaine | Alimentation humaine | Abattage | 2020 # profile method, budget smaller than the number of distinct profiles: # one strain in each of the 20 largest groups res_profile_20 <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 20, method = "profile", seed = 1) plot(res_profile_20)

title: Get started
text: define_profiles() builds profile strain concatenating columns binary table. Strains identical profiles put group; profile shared strain forms group single strain.
code: raw_data <- salmonella_strains prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),                                id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT") #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE upset_data <- prepare_upset(prepared_data) upset_profiles <- define_profiles(upset_data) # number of distinct profiles max(upset_profiles$group) #> [1] 61

title: Get started
text: Finally, select_profiles() selects one strain per group. group containing single strain gets strain; since strains larger group identical, one chosen random. Use seed make selection reproducible.
code: raw_data <- salmonella_strains prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),                                id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT") #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE upset_profiles <- define_profiles(prepare_upset(prepared_data)) selection <- select_profiles(upset_profiles, prepared_data, seed = 1) # one strain per distinct profile length(unique(selection$selected)) #> [1] 61

what: strainselect: Select Bacterial Strains to Sequence Based on Their Metadata — strainselect-package
title: strainselect: Select Bacterial Strains to Sequence Based on Their Metadata — strainselect-package
text: Helps choosing bacterial strains sequence collection described categorical metadata (sampling context, matrix, region, year...). Two methods provided. clustering method groups strains chosen number clusters using Gower distance hierarchical clustering, selects best clustered strain cluster according silhouette width; suited number strains can sequenced limited. profile method groups strains share exactly metadata selects one strain per group, every distinct profile represented.

title: strainselect: Select Bacterial Strains to Sequence Based on Their Metadata — strainselect-package
text: methods start prepare_input(), cleans table metadata. clustering method suited number strains can sequenced limited: assess_gower() computes Gower distances hierarchical clustering, cstats_table() helps choosing number clusters, select_silhouette() selects best clustered strain cluster. profile method suited number strains limited: prepare_upset() builds binary table modalities, define_profiles() groups strictly identical strains, select_profiles() selects one strain per group. See vignette("get-started", package = "strainselect") complete example.
